replies.text:
Permafrost does not prevent construction, it just makes it cost a bit more. Example, when building a road, we need to blast away all the permafrost we encounter with explosives and build a solid foundation for the road. Its like building a bridge over water. The foundation pillars are whats holding the road/bridge and they are anchored directly onto the bed rock beneath the permafrost. No matter how much the permafrost shifts, melts or reforms, it won't damage the road because the permafrost is not holding the road, its the pillars that are holding it. 
Canada is a lot more advanced then most think. Of course we don't build such roads everywhere, only the most important highways are built like that. For example, the railway upgrade that goes to Churchill is being built this way. 
Now as for farmland, Canada has a lot more then what is currently being farmed. Only the flat lands are being farmed as they are the easiest. But the Canadian Shield has the perfect conditions for farming too. It holds over 20% of the world's fresh water. There is over a million lakes in there. The soil is very fertile, but its small patches here and there. The land needs a lot of manual work. The soil needs to be gathered and terraces needs to be built to hold the soil in place so that farming on a large scale becomes possible. We could even have rice fields because fresh water that abondant. We just need to reshape the land into the shape of terraces. But almost no one wants to do it because Canada already produces too much food as it is.
